blocks.note: how a problem names the site it is about: `our` (40), the length a key is cut to, `IL`, which replaces what `y$'s pattern matches and answers the text unchanged while it fits, and `RAt` (10000), the length a string check refuses past
`QAe`, the allowed-keys predicate: every own key of an object is one of the listed ones

the checks both leaf problems run before their own: `EVe`, whether a leaf is stamped by a plugin of this chain (`plugin` a non-empty string), `xye`, a value that must be a string when given, within `RAt` characters and without a control character, and `XPn`, which sweeps a key list and answers the first problem it finds
`ace`, the same string check without the length cap — the one an alt or a label goes through, where `xye` is the one a key does
`H_` and `$_` (255 by 255), the size an Image is checked against, and `tL`, that check

`Bto`, the Image leaf problem: the props must be source/columns/rows/alt with a key when given, no children, and no other key at all — a leftover key is named in the message, because a press goes on an enclosing Button — then alt and key as strings, the size, the ImageSource shape `Mss`, and the stamp; the message is `Image "<key>" <problem>` or `Image <problem>`
`Gto`, the picker a Raster's props go through: an object whose `key` is a non-empty string and whose every other key is allowed, answered as a copy, or nothing at all

`Jto`, the Raster leaf problem: the props come from `Gto` against `Xto`, so a key and nothing else; no children; then the key sweep `XPn(["key"])`, the default size check `tF`, the cell decode `fur(cells, columns, rows)` — whose own problem is the message — and the stamp; the message is `Raster "<key>" <problem>`
